change_type: Configuration constant change affecting the permitted per-cycle brake-pressure increase
change_request: Reduce MAX_BRAKE_RISE_BAR_PER_CYCLE from 12.0 bar to 8.0 bar. Keep the existing behavior for requests at or below the measured pressure, and do not change the pressure-reduction path.
impact_summary: The shared limiter will cap pressure increases at 8.0 bar per cycle in both shown controller paths, rather than 12.0 bar. This can change the rate at which rising pressure commands are applied; the code context does not establish the control-cycle timing or any other consumers of the constant.
affected_callers: LimitBrakePressureRise reads MAX_BRAKE_RISE_BAR_PER_CYCLE when calculating the maximum allowed pressure.
AbsControllerStep calls LimitBrakePressureRise and passes its result to SetWheelPressure.
EbdControllerStep calls LimitBrakePressureRise and passes its result to SetWheelPressure.
downstream_logic: For a requested pressure above the allowed rise, LimitBrakePressureRise returns measured pressure plus the configured per-cycle increase; the upper bound changes from 12.0 bar to 8.0 bar.
Requests at or below measured pressure continue to be returned unchanged by the shown function.
Both controller steps pass the limited command to SetWheelPressure.
dependency_reasoning: The constant is used by LimitBrakePressureRise to calculate measured_bar plus the permitted rise. AbsControllerStep and EbdControllerStep both call that function and forward its result to SetWheelPressure, so both paths inherit the lower rising-pressure limit. The function returns requested_bar unchanged when the request is not above the calculated maximum; thus, as requested, the shown pressure-reduction behavior is unchanged.
review_recommendations: Test requests below, at, and above measured pressure plus 8.0 bar, and confirm the returned value never exceeds the new rising-pressure bound.
Verify requests at or below measured pressure are still passed through unchanged.
Exercise both AbsControllerStep and EbdControllerStep to confirm the limited command reaches SetWheelPressure.
Check other uses of the constant and verify the intended per-cycle limit against the configured control-cycle timing.
affected_control_functions: The ABS pressure-command path is affected when its requested pressure is more than 8.0 bar above the measured pressure in a cycle.
The EBD pressure-command path is affected under the same rising-pressure condition.

change_type: Logic change to the symmetric steering-angle saturation limits
change_request: Change ClampSteerRequest so that it clamps the requested steering angle to +450 mrad and -450 mrad instead of +540 mrad and -540 mrad. Preserve the sign of the request and leave downstream conversion behavior unchanged.
impact_summary: The change narrows the steering-angle command range to ±450 mrad along the shown path. Review the resulting rack-current behavior at and beyond both limits; the code context does not show other steering paths or the calibration of the angle-to-current conversion.
affected_callers: SteeringControlStep calls ClampSteerRequest and uses its result as the input to SteerAngleToRackCurrent.
ChassisControlTask is an indirect caller through SteeringControlStep; its steering request therefore reaches the revised clamp.
downstream_logic: The clamped angle is passed to SteerAngleToRackCurrent.
The resulting rack current is passed to PublishRackCurrent.
Requests outside the new limits are saturated before conversion; requests within the limits pass through unchanged.
dependency_reasoning: ClampSteerRequest is called directly by SteeringControlStep, which then converts the returned angle to rack current and publishes that current. ChassisControlTask supplies the request to SteeringControlStep, so it is affected indirectly. The source shows no other callers or control paths for the changed symbol. Since the requested change only alters the clamp bounds, downstream conversion and publication remain the same, while out-of-range requests produce different values.
review_recommendations: Test requests just below, at, and just above both new limits, plus values inside the range.
Verify positive and negative saturation are symmetric and preserve the request sign.
Confirm the angle-to-current conversion and published command behave as intended at the new endpoints.
Search for additional callers of ClampSteerRequest outside the provided context before merging.
affected_control_functions: Steering command authority is reduced for requests above 450 mrad or below -450 mrad, as represented by the steering request path in SteeringControlStep.
Rack-current command generation is affected for out-of-range requests because it receives the newly clamped angle.

change_type: Function interface and computation change: return type and output parameter change, with validity-filtered averaging and a minimum-valid-sample condition
change_request: Change EstimateVehicleSpeed to return bool and write the estimated speed through a float pointer parameter. Average only wheel samples whose valid flag is true, and return false when fewer than three samples are valid. Update every caller to handle the new signature and failure result.
impact_summary: This change affects the estimator interface, both shown callers, and the stability and cruise processing paths that consume its result. Correct failure handling is necessary to prevent downstream logic from using an estimate when the minimum valid-sample requirement is not met.
affected_callers: StabilityTask calls EstimateVehicleSpeed and must adopt the bool-plus-output-parameter interface and handle false before using the estimate.
CruiseTask calls EstimateVehicleSpeed and must adopt the new interface and handle false before invoking CruiseSpeedController.
downstream_logic: StabilityTask passes the estimated speed to UpdateYawReference and UpdateWheelSlip; these operations must not consume an invalid estimate when fewer than three wheel samples are valid.
CruiseTask passes the estimated speed to CruiseSpeedController; this call requires explicit handling of an estimation failure.
The estimate will be based only on samples marked valid rather than on all four wheel speeds.
dependency_reasoning: The source shows two direct callers, StabilityTask and CruiseTask. Both currently assume EstimateVehicleSpeed always returns a float and immediately pass it to downstream functions. The proposed bool return and output pointer require both callers to be updated; the specified failure condition also means each caller must decide what to do when fewer than three wheel samples are valid. The estimator currently averages all four speed fields without checking valid, so filtering by that flag changes the value supplied to both paths.
review_recommendations: Update both callers to the new signature and ensure neither downstream path uses the output when the function returns false.
Test zero, one, and two valid samples for failure, and three or four valid samples for a valid estimate.
Verify invalid wheel speeds do not contribute to the average and valid samples are weighted equally as specified.
Define and test the output-parameter state on failure so callers cannot accidentally use a stale estimate.
affected_control_functions: The stability path's yaw-reference and wheel-slip updates are affected because both consume the estimated vehicle speed.
The cruise speed-control path is affected because CruiseSpeedController consumes the estimated vehicle speed.
